cards.title: Math.max and Math.min
cards.body: `Math.max(4, 9, 2)` gives the biggest number. Put `...` before an array to pass its items: `Math.max(...nums)`.

hi.title: Math.max aur Math.min
hi.body: `Math.max(4, 9, 2)` sabse bada number deta hai. Array ke items bhejne ke liye uske aage `...` lagao: `Math.max(...nums)`.

cards.title: Spreading an array
cards.body: `...nums` spreads an array out into separate values, as if you had typed them one by one.

hi.title: Array ko spread karna
hi.body: `...nums` array ko alag alag values mein faila deta hai, jaise aapne unhe ek ek karke type kiya ho.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print 9, but prints `NaN`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `Math.max` wants separate numbers, not an array. Spread it: `Math.max(...nums)`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse 9 print karna chahiye, par yeh `NaN` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `Math.max` ko alag alag numbers chahiye, array nahi. Spread karo: `Math.max(...nums)`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Among negative numbers, the one closest to zero is the largest.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Negative numbers mein jo zero ke sabse paas hai, wahi sabse bada hai.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line, separated by spaces, and print the largest.
exercise.promptHi: Ek line mein spaces se alag kiye whole numbers padho aur sabse bada print karo.
exercise.starterCode:
